name: Edwardian Welsh (1277–1300)
source_notes: Caernarfon Castle (begun 1283): great polygonal towers, banded stonework and a strongly battered plinth; the curtain walls are roughly 2.4 m thick and 9–12 m high.
Conwy Castle (1283–1287): eight projecting round towers on a narrow rock ridge; walls and towers share a pronounced batter and a deep foundation plinth.
Harlech Castle (1283–1289): concentric curtain with tall round corner towers, a 2.4–3.0 m wall thickness and a gatehouse whose flanking towers command the approach.
Beaumaris Castle (begun 1295): the most regular Edwardian concentric plan, with a wide moat, low-battered curtain walls and evenly spaced flanking towers (roughly 25–42 m apart).
